Report_ID: Catheter occlusion during catheter dwell time (per catheter)
Title: Prospective Randomized Comparison of Valved Versus Nonvalved Peripherally Inserted Central Vein Catheters
Author: Hoffer EK, Borsa J, Santulli P, Bloch R, Fontaine AB
Comment: Abstract reports "The clamped and valved catheter groups had 13 and five occlusions, respectively (p = .06)", inconsistent with the Results text and Table 5 (six valved occlusions, p = .10); the Results/Table 5 values were extracted. Unit of analysis is catheters (362 catheters in 333 patients), not participants.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Clamped non-valved open-ended 5-French single-lumen PICC (Cook), heparin-saline flush') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Adult patients (>18 years, mean age 46, range 18-80) requiring single-lumen upper extremity PICC for therapy exceeding 7 days
Recruitment source: Interventional radiology service, Harborview Medical Center, Seattle, WA
Outcome measurement: Number of catheters with occlusion (inability to use catheter for assigned therapy) during dwell time; dichotomous events/total per arm
Outcome variable: Catheter occlusion during catheter dwell time (per catheter)

Report_ID: Catheter occlusion (partial and/or complete) during PICC dwell/treatment
Title: How Does Your PICCOMPARE? A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial Comparing Various PICC Materials in Pediatrics
Author: Kleidon TM, Ullman AJ, Zhang L, Mihala G, Chaseling B, Schoutrop J, Rickard CM
Comment: Events are the SUM of the paper's separately reported partial (11 vs 5) and complete (10 vs 2) occlusion counts during treatment; Table 2 footnote states more than 1 complication per patient is possible, so these sums may double-count patients and represent an upper bound (21/74 and 7/72). No p-value was reported for the individual occlusion rows. Intervention arm differs from control in both valve (PASV®) and material (Endexo®), so the valve effect is confounded with catheter material.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Standard care: Cook™ polyurethane turbo-ject power-injectable PICC with external clamp (non-valved)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Pediatric patients (<18 years) requiring a single-lumen PICC
Recruitment source: Lady Cilento Children's Hospital, South Brisbane, Queensland, Australia (tertiary pediatric teaching hospital)
Outcome measurement: Number of patients/PICCs with occlusion recorded as a complication during treatment (partial 11 vs 5; complete 10 vs 2)
Outcome variable: Catheter occlusion (partial and/or complete) during PICC dwell/treatment

Report_ID: Catheter occlusion during dwell time (catheters occluded at least once)
Title: The effect of peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC) valve technology on catheter occlusion rates - The 'ELeCTRiC' study
Author: Johnston AJ, Streater CT, Noorani R, Crofts JL, Del Mundo AB, Parker RA
Comment: Valved arms combined by extractor (paper reports them separately); no pooled non-valved-vs-valved effect estimate is reported by the paper. Trial stopped early (102 of 300 planned) and one PASV patient was excluded from analysis, so analysed total is 101 while Table I/II still list PASV n=33. The paper's reported CI '11% (95% CI, 11% to 32%)' appears to contain a typographical sign error and refers to Cook/Groshong vs PASV, not non-valved vs valved; it was therefore not recorded as an effect estimate.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Cook Medical non-valved open-ended Turbo-Flo dual lumen 5 Fr PICC') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: adult ICU patients (age ≥18) referred for PICC insertion
Recruitment source: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust intensive care unit, Vascular Access Team referrals
Outcome measurement: Number of catheters/patients with at least one occlusion out of total randomized per arm; valved arms (Groshong 13/34 + PASV 9/33) combined into a single valved comparator = 22/67
Outcome variable: Catheter occlusion during dwell time (catheters occluded at least once)
additional_group_ns: Arms as reported separately: Cook non-valved n=34 (13 occluded, 38%); Groshong n=34 (13 occluded, 38%); PASV n=33 (9 occluded, 27%). The two valved arms were combined by the extractor into one comparator (22/67) per the synthesis plan; no other arms excluded.

Report_ID: Catheter lumen occlusion (irreversible + transient + partial withdrawal occlusion)
Title: A prospective, randomized comparison of three different types of valved and non-valved peripherally inserted central catheters
Author: Pittiruti M, Emoli A, Porta P, Marche B, DeAngelis R, Scoppettuolo G
Comment: Per-arm occlusion totals summed across the three Table II occlusion rows (irreversible + transient + PWO); the paper reports only counts with no p-value or effect measure for this comparison. Assumes each occlusion episode occurred in a distinct catheter (8 episodes, 8 catheters implied by narrative). Unit of analysis = patients/catheters (one PICC per patient).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Non-valved power-injectable PICC (ProPICC, Medcomp)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: adult oncologic outpatients receiving intermittent chemotherapy via 4Fr single-lumen PICC
Recruitment source: Day Hospital of Oncology, Catholic University Hospital, Rome
Outcome measurement: Number of PICCs with any occlusion episode during dwell time (events/total per arm); valved arms (Solo-2 and PASV) combined
Outcome variable: Catheter lumen occlusion (irreversible + transient + partial withdrawal occlusion)
additional_group_ns: Valved comparator formed by combining the two valved arms: Solo valve n=61 (1 irreversible + 2 transient + 1 PWO = 4 events); PASV n=60 (1 transient = 1 event)

Title: A comparison of hydrophobic polyurethane and polyurethane peripherally inserted central catheter: results from a feasibility randomized controlled trial
Author: Gavin NC, Kleidon TM, Larsen E, O'Brien C, Ullman A, Northfield S, Mihala G, Runnegar N, Marsh N, Rickard CM
Comment: Percentages in Table 2 (60% and 55%) are column percentages of the 45 patients who had any complication during treatment, not of group size; event counts 15 and 11 are against analysed group totals of 55 per arm (Table 3). No formal statistical test was reported for occlusion. Note the paper's intervention arm (valved) is the review's comparator; arms also differ in catheter material, confounding the valve comparison.
Participant type: Adult hospital inpatients (>=18 years) requiring a PICC for fluid or medication administration
Recruitment source: Department of Medical Imaging, Royal Brisbane and Women's Hospital, and Hospital in the Home service
Outcome measurement: Number of participants with occlusion / total randomised and analysed per arm
